column1: # scripts/bash-shard-costs.tsv — the MEASURED cost of each shard, in seconds, for the slice assignment
# in `scripts/run-bash-shards.sh` (agent-infra#4210).
# FORMAT: `<seconds><TAB><path>`, one shard per line, `#` comments and blank lines ignored. A shard
# absent from this file still RUNS — it is weighted at the MEDIAN of the measured ones, and the run
# prints how many fell back, so a stale table is visible instead of silently re-clustering the heavy
# suites. A malformed row (non-numeric seconds, no path) is skipped rather than guessed at.
# WHY A TABLE AT ALL: the assignment bin-packs by cost (LPT). With no table every shard weighs the same
# and the deal is the POSITIONAL round-robin it replaced (`pos % n`) — correct, and cost-blind. The
# table is what makes "the heavy suites land on different CI arms" true instead of lucky.
# PROVENANCE: the per-suite `▸ <secs> <path>` rows of daniel-ospina/agent-infra's own
# `ci-main.yml` runs, NEWEST RUN WINS per path. Base = run 45284947925 (head 1d048d3722aa, 2026-11-23),
# filled from run 45107109343 for the shards whose arms were killed before they reported. Two shards
# never reported in any sampled run (`scripts/pi-reap-idle.test.sh`, `scripts/reap-landed-worktrees.test.sh`)
# were measured locally on the same day.
# REFRESH — when a suite is added, or the numbers drift enough that `▸` rows disagree with this file:
#   gh run list --repo daniel-ospina/agent-infra --workflow ci-main.yml --branch main --limit 3 \
#     --json databaseId --jq '.[].databaseId' \
#   | while read -r run; do
#       gh run view "$run" --repo daniel-ospina/agent-infra --json jobs \
#         --jq '.jobs[] | select(.name|test("script-validate \\(")) | .databaseId'
#     done \
#   | while read -r job; do
#       gh run view --repo daniel-ospina/agent-infra --job "$job" --log 2>/dev/null \
#     done | awk -F'\t' '!seen[$2]++' | sort -rn > /tmp/costs.tsv   # then replace the body below
# ⚠️ STALENESS IS BOUNDED, NOT ELIMINATED: the costs are a snapshot and the list grows. What keeps that
# honest is arithmetic, not discipline — each run prints `🧮 … this arm models Ns, worst arm Ns` against
# the declared step bound, and says so loudly (⚠️ CAPACITY) when the worst arm no longer fits. A table
# that is merely old degrades the packing; it never drops a suite, and it never reds a run.
